operating_point.platform: CPU: a GitHub runner (4 vCPU; one CPU and one BLAS thread pinned for the bit comparison)
operating_point.sizes_and_parameters: the walk: every registered node class in the switch scan's configurations (302 steps, float64, with the plants on the six cases of tests/solve_sites in both dtypes); the bits: the near field at two and three spheres of 1 mm a gap of 0.3 mm apart at a force spacing of 0.6 mm on the dense route and on GMRES, the open box, the FVM's three schemes, script A and its body, the rigid body's kept form, the RFT drag in the tube, the dynamic arm with and without mass, the lubricated sphere and ellipsoid, the arm-tracking controller in the graph, each run 20 ms; and the gradient of the sum of the near field's final state in the water viscosity through 3 steps
operating_point.seeds_and_draws: no draws: a traced program is deterministic, so a control's rate across processes shows the harness (the process, its seed, its thread layout), not independent draws; 30 is one observation repeated, not 30 samples

gate_1_walk_reach.claim: every registered node class's step is traced by some switch configuration, and no step holds a solve primitive outside a registered scope, nested in a scope that does not own it, or over an exempt site's size bound; the registry and the walk agree both ways on which node class reaches which site

prediction.unit: problems found over 302 steps of 43 node classes
prediction.why: after the routing every solve of the inventory sits in a scope, and the sites' kinds own the primitives the inventory found in them (the dense scope holds lu, triangular_solve and custom_linear_solve; the Cholesky site cholesky and triangular_solve; the CG custom_linear_solve; the GMRES custom_linear_solve and triangular_solve; the transform fft)

gate_1_walk_reach.metric: the findings of solve_problems over every step, per node class

control.plant: nested_in_cg (a raw 8 x 8 solve in the CG's operator) and inside_exempt (a raw 30 x 30 solve inside the six-unknown blocks' scope), tests/solve_sites/solve_walk.py
control.expected_rate: 30/30 each, in float64 and in float32 on the first case
control.resolution: one solve primitive anywhere in a step, however nested

gate_1_walk_reach.if_wrong: a solve the inventory missed: register it or route it, and report which
gate_1_walk_reach.cannot_discriminate_if: a node class none of the configurations builds: the test fails for such a class by name, so it cannot pass silently; a solve in a branch none of the configurations takes is outside the walk, and the rule says so

gate_2_forms.claim: a least squares, a pseudo-inverse and a tridiagonal solve added to a node's step are found, as a raw solve is
gate_2_forms.case: the same direct-solve plant with the form changed, on the FVM tube's steady step and the near field's dense step

prediction.why: lstsq and pinv trace svd and tridiagonal_solve traces its own primitive, all now in SOLVE_PRIMITIVES; the review measured 0/10 before

gate_2_forms.metric: the findings text names the primitive outside every scope

control.resolution: one such solve of any order

gate_2_forms.if_wrong: a form whose primitive is not in the set: add it
gate_2_forms.cannot_discriminate_if: a bare loop of matrix products (a Jacobi fori_loop) or an eigh: neither has a solve primitive, and the rule says so rather than claiming them

gate_3_dtype.claim: in a float64 run no equation of a node's step holds a narrower float, so a float32 round trip completed in the caller before dense_solve and an answer rounded through float32 after it are both found, as a downcast inside a scope is; the Poisson transform's scope is held to the same
gate_3_dtype.case: the dense plants on the near field's dense step and the open box, and a downcast inside the Poisson transform on the three FVM steps, float64

prediction.why: the walk reads every equation of the step, not only those inside a scope; the review measured zero narrower floats in all six float64 cases, so the clean arm is quiet

gate_3_dtype.metric: an equation of the step holding float32

control.resolution: one float32 round trip of one value

gate_3_dtype.if_wrong: a node kind that legitimately holds float32 outside its solve: declare it narrower with its reason, as the arm-tracking controller is
gate_3_dtype.cannot_discriminate_if: a float32 run (x64 off): the dtype walk is float64 only; the scope and ownership checks are run in float32 as well

gate_4_bounds.claim: an exempt site's size bound is checked on the operands the walk traces: the bound set one below the largest system the walk traces in the site is found, for each of the four exempt sites
gate_4_bounds.case: the switch configurations that trace each site (mrs_point_forces for the per-body solve, dynamic_rpm for the arm's Cholesky, the in-graph tracked controller for the IK's, mrs_near_field for the own blocks)

prediction.why: the largest order is read off the same trace and the bound is planted one below it, so the walk must find the equation that has that order

gate_4_bounds.metric: the finding names the exempt site and its bound

control.plant: bound:<site> in probe/walk_once.py (a declaration planted: the registry with one site's bound one below the largest order traced in it)

gate_4_bounds.if_wrong: an order read from the wrong operand: matrix primitives carry their order in the first operand's last dimension
gate_4_bounds.cannot_discriminate_if: a site whose steps trace no matrix primitive: the test requires the premise (a matrix inside the site)
